note_on_method: One of the five filter slugs has a lawful data driver in San Antonio. Outdoor does, because the City writes the word into its count sentence at six of the eight published venues. Indoor has one venue, Palm Heights, and lights has two, Fairchild and Tejeda: real answers, both under the three-venue threshold for a page. Free has no driver because the City never states a price.

slots.why_this_filter:
Thirty-five of San Antonio's forty-three courts are stated outdoor, at six parks, and the reason this page exists is the word itself. Most operators in this directory count courts and leave a reader to assume they are outside; San Antonio writes "outdoor" into the count sentence: "There are 18 lighted, outdoor pickleball courts." at Fairchild, "There are eight outdoor pickleball courts." at Monterrey, "There is one outdoor pickleball court." at Oak Haven, and is one of the few operators here that does. That is what lets this page say thirty-five rather than "probably all of them".

The distribution is lopsided. Fairchild holds eighteen of the thirty-five, lit, on the east side; Monterrey eight on the west side; Normoyle four on the south-west side; Garza and Pittman-Sullivan two each; Oak Haven one on the north side.

Only Fairchild's eighteen are under stated lights. At the other five parks the City's caveat, "Some courts are not lighted.", is the final word, so an outdoor court in San Antonio is a daylight court by default unless it is at Fairchild. Park hours run 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily everywhere, which is generous but not the same as usable after dark. The City states no surface anywhere, and no price.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the City of San Antonio states an outdoor pickleball court count for it on the park's own page, and the word "outdoor" has to be the City's. Six qualify: Fairchild Park (18), Monterrey Park (8), Normoyle Park (4), Garza Park (2), Pittman-Sullivan Park (2) and Oak Haven Park (1), thirty-five courts in all.

Two published venues do not. Palm Heights Park's courts are indoors, "There are 2 indoor pickleball courts.", which is an answer rather than a gap. Tejeda Park's sentence reads "There are 6 lighted, pickleball courts." and never says outdoor, so its six are left off; a reader who wants Tejeda will find it on the city page with its lighting answer intact.

Piazza Italia Park would qualify if it could be located. Its page says "There is one outdoor pickleball court.", but its address, "500 Columbus" is found by neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap.

faqs.q: Why is Tejeda Park not on this page?
faqs.a: Its sentence is "There are 6 lighted, pickleball courts.", with no "outdoor", where every other park page has one. This site does not complete the City's sentences, so Tejeda's breakdown stays unstated.
Fairchild Park's eighteen, on the City's own words. At the other five outdoor venues the City says nothing about pickleball lighting, so they are recorded as unknown.
Not stated. "First come, first served" is the City's play format, not a price, and no page states a charge or the absence of one.

sources.publisher: City of San Antonio Parks & Recreation
sources.evidence: The City's pickleball directory page. Intro: "There are several indoor and outdoor pickleball courts at our parks across the city. These are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Some courts are not lighted." Then "Courts at Hamilton Community Center are available Saturday, 10 a.m. - 2 p.m." and "All other courts are available during park hours." and "Want to learn how to play? Take a Pickleball 101 class through the Fitness in the Park program, equipment provided." Under "Directory" it says "11 Result(s) Found" and lists ten entries, each park with its address and "Park Hours: Sunday - Saturday: 5 a.m. - 11 p.m."; Normoyle Park additionally "Pool Hours: Saturday & Sunday: 1 - 8 p.m."; Hamilton Community Center at "10700 Nacogdoches Rd., San Antonio, TX 78217" with "Facility Hours: Monday - Thursday: 10 a.m. - 8 p.m. Friday: 2 - 6 p.m. Saturday: 10 a.m. - 4 p.m." and no count; Piazza Italia Park at "500 Columbus, San Antonio, TX 78207". "Page 1 of 2", and page two returns the same ten. Snapshot: data/sources/san-antonio/pickleball.html
sources.not_stated: Any court count, any price, any surface, which courts are the unlit ones, and the eleventh result.

sources.publisher: City of San Antonio Parks & Recreation
sources.evidence: Tejeda Park's page. Park History: "The 8.7570 acres of property for this park were purchased in 1977. The park was originally called Division Park for the street on which it is located, but was renamed for Congressman Frank Tejeda by ordinance of City Council passed on Sept. 12, 1996." Tejeda "was a U.S. Marine and Vietnam veteran who earned the Bronze Star for valor and the Purple Heart", "earned a masters from Harvard University and his law degree from Yale", served in the Texas House from 1977, the Texas Senate from 1987, and the U.S. House for District 28 from 1993; "He died of brain cancer on Jan. 30, 1997". Featured Amenities: "Pickleball Courts: There are 6 lighted, pickleball courts." "Tennis Courts: The tennis courts are lighted." Softball Field for rental. Amenity list includes Bleachers, Dugouts, Handicapped Parking Spaces, Regular Parking Spaces, Restrooms, Tennis Court. Address "541 Division Ave. San Antonio, TX 78214". Hours "Sunday - Saturday: 5 a.m. - 11 p.m." Snapshot: data/sources/san-antonio/tejeda-park.html
sources.not_stated: Whether the pickleball courts are outdoor or indoor, price, surface, and parking capacity.
